elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Amended Section 14: "...until the last day of the month following the month in which Client provides TrueLink with a written notice of its election to terminate this Agreement for convenience, without cause." The deterministic check "Customer convenience termination present" returned false because the text never uses a direct "Client may terminate" formulation; in substance, however, the section is captioned TERMINATION and its whole mechanic runs off Client's unilateral election, which is now expressly for convenience and without cause, so the right exists in operative text (a direct grant would be cleaner but is not required for this element).

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: Termination takes effect only on "the last day of the month following the month in which Client provides ... written notice" \u2014 i.e. roughly 31 to 60 days depending on the day of the month notice is given. No thirty (30) day notice figure is stated for Client's Section 14 exit (the 30-day figure in Section 13 is non-renewal notice, not convenience termination). To reach preferred the drafter must make Client's termination effective "thirty (30) days after Client's written notice."

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: No refund language appears in the rendered text. Section 5(a) only provides monthly invoicing with "Invoices will be paid within 15 days of receipt"; that neither creates a refund obligation nor rules out prepayment for a partial period. To reach preferred, insert: "TrueLink shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination."

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: After the redline TrueLink's only no-cause exit is non-renewal effective at the end of the one-year period, on ninety (90) days' notice. The mid-term proviso terminating "Sections 2 and 3" is triggered only by Client breach/default or breach of Sections 8a-8c (for cause), and Section 14 confers the election on Client alone. Residual drafting point: the surviving cross-reference "until terminated pursuant to Section 12 herein" appears to be a mis-reference (Section 12 is indemnity/liability cap per the drafter's check) and should be corrected to Section 14 to remove any argument that it is an undefined termination trigger.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Amended Section 14 gives Client an express "election to terminate this Agreement for convenience, without cause," with services running to the last day of the month following the notice month (~30-60 days). That is a shorter notice burden than the 60-90 day fallback ceiling and therefore betters the element; the element tests the maximum notice Customer must give, so a shorter period is favourable and is not a defect.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: no early-termination fee, penalty, liquidated damage or unamortised-cost charge appears anywhere in the cited or rendered text. Section 5(a) charges only monthly invoices for services actually requested, payable 15 days after receipt, so on termination Client's exposure is at most the current month \u2014 well inside a three-month cap. Note the mapping labels this "already_met" by quoting Section 5(a); strictly it is met because no ETF exists, not because that quote imposes a cap.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Amended Section 13 leaves TrueLink with a non-renewal notice only, operating "prior to the end of said year," so its no-cause exit lands at the end of the annual term; the only mid-term terminations available against Client are the for-cause proviso triggers (breach of System/Credit Repository Agreements or Sections 8a-8c).

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Amended Section 13: "...or TrueLink delivers such notice no later than ninety (90) days, prior to the end of said year." "No later than ninety (90) days prior to the end" operates as a floor of ninety days' advance notice, replacing the prior 30-day vendor notice that sat in the walk-away band. "Such notice" refers unambiguously back to "written notice of intent not to renew."

reasons: Fallback level is complete: all four fallback elements are met in the rendered operative text \u2014 Client's exit is now expressly for convenience/without cause on ~30-60 days (better than the 60-90 day ceiling), no early-termination fee exists so the three-month cap is bettered, and TrueLink's only no-cause exit is non-renewal at the end of the term on ninety (90) days' notice.

Preferred is correctly not claimed and fails on two elements: (i) Client's termination is effective on the last day of the month following the notice month (up to ~60 days) rather than a flat thirty (30) days, and (ii) there is no pro-rata refund of prepaid fees. If the drafter wants preferred, add "effective thirty (30) days after Client's written notice" and "TrueLink shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination."

The deterministic check "Customer convenience termination present" returned false; on inspection this reflects drafting form, not substance \u2014 Section 14 confers the exit indirectly (TrueLink must continue services until the date fixed by Client's election). Optional hardening, not required for the fallback: recast as "Client may terminate this Agreement for convenience, without cause, upon written notice, and TrueLink will continue to provide the Services until the last day of the month following the month of such notice," so the grant is a direct operative right rather than an inference from a wind-down obligation.

Minimal: only two surgical edits were made \u2014 inserting "for convenience, without cause" in Section 14 and splitting the Section 13 non-renewal notice into Client 30 days / TrueLink 90 days. Client's favourable 30-day non-renewal notice, the wind-down periods (30-day name server, 60-day hosting environment), domain ownership and the for-cause proviso are all retained, no operative term is duplicated and nothing outside the T4C checklist is added.

Preserves intent: payment and invoicing mechanics (Section 5(a)), the one-year auto-renewing term, the "Subject to Section 4" qualifier and all remedies survive unchanged, and the amended renewal sentence remains grammatically coherent with no internal contradiction.

Two residual items to tidy in a follow-up pass (neither blocks the fallback): correct the stale cross-reference "until terminated pursuant to Section 12 herein" (Section 12 is indemnity/liability; Section 14 is termination) so no undefined termination trigger survives, and confirm that the Section 4 minimum support period does not delay Client's Section 14 convenience exit beyond the notice mechanic.
